correctness.rationale: The Rota–Baxter bilinear identity on (v,v) forces the scalar part of P(V) to vanish, and its scalar part on (1,1) forces the scalar part of P(1) to vanish. The remaining equations (1,v) and (1,1) are exactly L^2=0 and 2L(u)=0; all other pairs follow by bilinearity, proving equivalence for arbitrary fields. P^2(a+v)=aL(u) and P^3=0 are exact. A rank-r square-zero matrix corresponds bijectively to image U contained in kernel W and an isomorphism V/W to U, giving the stated Gaussian coefficient. Verified by exhaustive original-identity testing of 16+81+512+19683+65536+262144 candidate operators over F2/F3/F4, matching all predictions. Experiment is not the general proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The obvious equivalent form is a block matrix with zero scalar row, square-zero radical block, and no restriction on its first column in characteristic two; equivalently P^3=0 and P^2(A) contained in V. Farooq has the same block setup but needs L(u)=0 and assumes characteristic zero, so the new extra freedom cannot be recovered by equivalent notation. The exterior algebra is not a specialization of the square-zero family for two generators because its radical square is nonzero.

originality.rationale: The closest same-algebra result (Farooq 2026 Theorem 3.4) explicitly works in characteristic zero and imposes P^2=0. The present characteristic-two family allows P^2!=0 and supplies complete finite-field index/rank enumerators, neither implied by Farooq under his field restriction. Gubarev (2021) likewise states general nilpotency under characteristic-zero hypotheses. The closest retrieved characteristic-two operator census concerns exterior algebra with nonzero square of radical rather than radical-square-zero algebras. No covering formula found in actual literature/record searches; historical equivalent formulations remain a qualified originality risk.
residual_risks: Prior treatment using a different Rota–Baxter or differential-operational terminology may be unindexed by the searches.

value.rationale: The full characteristic-two family differs structurally from the characteristic-zero theorem: its maximal nilpotency index jumps sharply from two to three beginning at radical dimension two. The exact q-binomial rank/index counts determine natural global invariants for the entire first-order local-algebra family over every finite field, with reproducible formulas and meaningful characteristic-sensitive boundaries; not just one finite census.
